name: CroissantMiner
description: CroissantMiner is a benchmark for extracting MLCommons Croissant metadata from ML dataset papers. It contains human-validated gold values for 102 datasets x 30 Croissant fields (3,060 cells) from 9,595 ratings by 22 annotators, with the raw ratings, calibration ratings, per-field agreement and a pseudonymized annotator roster; LLM-generated silver annotations for 500 further papers; the outputs of the 24 extraction systems and the reference system in the paper, with the GLM-5 judge verdicts behind its results; the judge audit (selection on 60 cells and a 200-cell human audit); and the re-annotation pilot used to check the effect of the seed model. This is version 1.2.0, the version the paper's results use; the version reviewed at NeurIPS 2026 (1.0.0) is tag v1.0 of this repository and is also kept unchanged at huggingface.co/datasets/croissantminer/croissantminer. Released under CC BY 4.0; LLM-generated text is subject to the providers' terms.
citeAs: @inproceedings{arda2026croissantminer, title={CroissantMiner: Automated Extraction and Validation of Croissant Metadata for ML Datasets}, author={Arda, Berke and Yavuz, Ahmetcan and Gerry, Paul and Lobentanzer, Sebastian and Sarwar, Nobin and Giner-Miguelez, Joan and Chen, Kongtao and Zhang, Luyao and Sachan, Mrinmaya and Akhtar, Mubashara}, booktitle={Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (Evaluations and Datasets Track)}, year={2026}}

recordSet.name: annotators
recordSet.description: Pseudonymized roster of the 22 annotators who contributed to the main set. Demographics aggregated from the recruitment registration form: coarse role, ML familiarity, paper-experience frequency, hours dedicated. No personally identifying information beyond what annotators publicly associate with their professional profiles.

recordSet.name: calibration
recordSet.description: Pilot ratings collected before the main collection began. Used a binary TRUE/FALSE rubric (mapped to rating 1 or 3 in this file) on a 15-cell sample. Released for transparency; downstream evaluation should use ratings.parquet.

recordSet.name: gold
recordSet.description: Derived gold values, one row per (paper, field). Computed by majority vote across raters (3 to 4 raters per cell, see n_raters column); cells where no rating reached majority (gold_method = 'tie_split') were sent to senior adjudication and the gold_value/gold_rating were filled by the adjudicator.

recordSet.name: iaa
recordSet.description: Per-field inter-annotator agreement metrics with bootstrap 95 percent confidence intervals. Reports Krippendorff's alpha (ordinal), Gwet's AC1 (chance-corrected, prevalence-robust), raw pairwise agreement, and percent unanimous cells. The AC1 + pairwise pair triangulates against the prevalence paradox in alpha when ratings cluster on one category.

recordSet.name: judge_audit_200
recordSet.description: Human audit of the deployed judge on 200 RAI cells: ratings by two authors (R1, R2), the third author's rating on their disagreements (R3), the human consensus and the GLM-5 score.

recordSet.name: judge_selection
recordSet.description: Judge selection: 60 development cells (30 calibration, 30 validation) with the human consensus rating and the scores of the six candidate judges under the initial rubric, plus GLM-5 under the final rubric on audited gold.

recordSet.name: judge_verdicts
recordSet.description: GLM-5 judge verdicts on the RAI fields behind the paper's results (score 1 = correct, 2 = partially correct, 3 = wrong), with the judge's reason; source marks verdicts added for the camera-ready.

recordSet.name: pilot_gold
recordSet.description: Re-annotation pilot: gold values from a GPT-5.4 pre-fill rated by three raters, for 15 papers; in_paper_analysis marks the 10 papers with three ratings on every field, used in the paper.

recordSet.name: pilot_ratings
recordSet.description: Re-annotation pilot: individual ratings (slot A, B or C per paper) with failure modes, corrections, confidence and notes.

recordSet.name: ratings
recordSet.description: Long-format raw human ratings, one row per (paper, field, annotator). Annotators were instructed to rate each LLM-extracted Croissant metadata value as Correct (1), Partially Correct (2), or Not Correct (3); for ratings of 2 or 3, an optional corrected_value and free-text notes were collected, plus a confidence label (High / Medium / Low) and a failure-mode category.

recordSet.name: silver
recordSet.description: Silver split: 500 ML dataset papers with paper-level metadata (arXiv ID, downloads, domain, license, tasks, language, datePublished, dataCollectionType). LLM-derived from arXiv metadata + Claude Sonnet 4.5 pre-fill at temperature 0; not human-validated. Used for scale studies and silver-vs-gold validation in the paper.

recordSet.name: silver_annotations
recordSet.description: LLM-generated silver annotations: the Claude Sonnet 4.5 pre-fill for 500 ML dataset papers x 30 Croissant fields (one row per paper and field). Not human-validated.

recordSet.name: system_outputs
recordSet.description: Outputs of the 24 extraction systems ranked in the paper and the Claude Sonnet 4.5 reference, one row per system, paper and field, on the 14 development and 88 test datasets.

rai:dataCollection: Human ratings of LLM-extracted Croissant metadata across 102 ML datasets and 30 Croissant fields (10 core and 20 RAI). Collected over seven phases between March and April 2026: pilot calibration, Phase 2 main collection, mid-project redistribution to balance coverage, a round-3 top-up, two final sweeps for cells under the three-rater target, and an orphan top-up to bring every cell to at least three distinct annotators. Senior adjudication resolved cells where no rating reached majority.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator. Annotators were instructed not to use AI tools while rating.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: AI-extracted Croissant metadata values produced by Claude Sonnet 4.5 on 102 arXiv-published ML dataset papers, plus the papers themselves (read by annotators when validating each value).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each (paper, field) cell received at least three independent ratings (four for 415 cells) on a three-level rubric (Correct / Partially Correct / Not Correct) with six failure-mode categories (Incomplete, Hallucination, Wrong Section, Granularity Mismatch, Format Error, Other) and an optional corrected value plus free-text notes. Confidence (High / Medium / Low) was recorded per rating.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Shared online spreadsheets, one per annotator and phase, with the rating instructions included.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Krippendorff's alpha (ordinal, primary), Gwet's AC1 (chance-corrected, prevalence-robust), raw pairwise agreement, and percent unanimous cells, all computed per field with 1000-iteration bootstrap 95 percent confidence intervals. Triangulation across alpha and AC1 is necessary because alpha collapses under skewed marginals (Feinstein-Cicchetti paradox).
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 ratings per cell; 4 for 415 of the 3,060 gold cells
rai:annotatorDemographics: 22 distinct annotators after deduplicating two who registered twice and merging name variants. Roles spanned PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, faculty, and industry professionals across academic and external institutions. Aggregate demographics in annotators.parquet (coarse role, ML familiarity tier, paper-experience frequency, hours dedicated). No personally identifying demographic data (age, gender, ethnicity, geography) was collected.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: None. Annotators were instructed not to use AI tools while rating. The pre-filled metadata values rated by annotators were generated by Claude Sonnet 4.5 (not part of the rating step itself).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Maintained by the authors at https://huggingface.co/datasets/bearda/croissantminer, with code at https://github.com/berkearda/croissantminer. Each version is a Git tag of this Hugging Face repository and can be loaded with revision="<tag>". v1.0 (7 May 2026) is the version reviewed at NeurIPS 2026; it is also kept unchanged at https://huggingface.co/datasets/croissantminer/croissantminer. v1.1 (28 September 2026) added the system outputs, judge verdicts, judge selection and audit, silver annotations and the re-annotation pilot. v1.2 (1 October 2026) is the version on the main branch and the one the paper's results use; its gold values are the same as in v1.0. Corrections to the data are released as new tagged versions and never overwrite an earlier version. Changes that touch only descriptions in this file or in the dataset card are made on the main branch without a new version. Documentation update of 5 November 2026: the descriptions, source papers and provenance in this file and the dataset card were corrected against the original records; the data files are unchanged and are still v1.2. Problems can be reported as GitHub issues.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators appear only as pseudonyms (A01 to A22). annotators.parquet gives, for each pseudonym, a coarse role, familiarity with ML datasets, paper-experience frequency, hours dedicated, the phases they took part in and their number of ratings; this is experience and seniority information. No annotator names, e-mail addresses, affiliations, age, gender, ethnicity or location are released. The judge-audit raters are three of the authors, labelled R1 to R3, and pilot raters appear only as slots A, B and C. Adjudicators are coded (A_senior_01, A_senior_02). Metadata values quote or summarise the public source papers, so they contain the names of those papers' authors (for example in creator and citeAs values) and a few contact e-mail addresses printed in the papers. No other personal or sensitive information is included.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables study of LLM extraction quality on Responsible AI metadata. Permits downstream research into RAI-field difficulty, extraction-distillation, and disagreement-aware fine-tuning. Limitation: source papers are arXiv-published English-language ML dataset papers, so coverage is biased toward the English-speaking ML research community.
rai:dataBiases: Annotator pool is biased toward ML/AI researchers (recruited via an open call to NeurIPS-track-adjacent researchers); ratings reflect this group's interpretation of the Croissant RAI rubric. Source-paper sample is biased toward Vision and NLP domains (the two largest fractions of the 102-paper benchmark). Field difficulty is non-uniform: short-text fields (sc:license, sc:datePublished) saw substantially higher pairwise agreement than long-form RAI fields (rai:dataBiases, rai:dataSocialImpact).
rai:dataLimitations: Three RAI field definitions (rai:dataCollectionMissingData, rai:dataManipulationProtocol, rai:dataBiases) were tightened in the annotator rubric beyond the canonical Croissant RAI 1.0 specification, which contributes to definitional asymmetry on rai:dataBiases between LLM extractions and human ratings. Annotator demographics are aggregate-only; no per-annotator demographic stratification of agreement is released. Source-paper PDFs are not redistributed; downstream users must obtain them from the original publishers.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Benchmarking of LLM-based metadata extraction systems for Responsible AI documentation. Suitable for evaluating extraction accuracy, abstention calibration (when fields are absent from a paper), and field-specific difficulty profiles.
rai:isSyntheticData: False. Annotations are human ratings produced by 22 annotators on real LLM-generated extractions of real published academic papers; no synthetic generation step is part of the annotation pipeline. The 500-paper silver split contains LLM-generated metadata, but the metadata itself is grounded in real source papers rather than synthesised from scratch.
rai:sourceDatasets: The 102 gold entries and the 500 silver entries are Hugging Face datasets, prioritising highly downloaded ones, each with a publicly available ML dataset paper: the gold entries were curated by hand, and the silver entries were selected automatically by download count. Some gold entries are different Hugging Face datasets described by the same paper. Each source paper is listed in prov:wasDerivedFrom with the entries it covers; the silver papers' arXiv identifiers are also in silver.parquet (arxiv_id). Paper PDFs are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original publishers (mostly arXiv).
rai:provenanceActivities: Provenance: (1) The gold source papers were picked by hand and their PDFs obtained between October 2025 and January 2026; the silver papers were selected automatically and their PDFs obtained in April 2026. (2) Claude Sonnet 4.5 pre-filled all 30 fields, for the gold entries in January 2026 and for the silver entries in April 2026 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, temperature 0, canonical prompt with SHA-256 prefix 1e1cfdd99246bbf5); the January run did not log its settings. (3) Human ratings were collected from 22 annotators between March and April 2026 across seven phases. (4) Gold values were derived by majority vote per (paper, field) cell, with senior-author adjudication for tie-split cells. (5) An end-to-end author audit in May 2026 corrected 191 of 3,060 gold cells (gold_method = 'audit_corrected_2026-05-04').

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Source paper selection
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: The corpus was built from publicly available ML dataset papers linked from Hugging Face datasets, prioritising highly downloaded datasets. The 102 gold entries were curated by hand across modalities and formats; some of them are different datasets described by the same paper. Their PDFs were obtained between October 2025 and January 2026 from arXiv and, for a few entries, from the publisher (ACL Anthology, ISCA Archive, a University of Toronto technical report and a Scale AI report). The 500 silver entries were selected automatically in April 2026 from Hugging Face datasets that link to an arXiv paper, ranked by download count, deduplicated by arXiv identifier and filtered to remove overlap with the gold split; their PDFs were obtained from arXiv in April 2026. The PDFs are not redistributed.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: LLM pre-fill of the gold entries
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Claude Sonnet 4.5 filled all 30 fields of each of the 102 gold entries on 7 and 13 January 2026; the run did not log its settings. These pre-fills are the values the annotators rated.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: LLM pre-fill of the silver entries
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) filled all 30 fields of each of the 500 silver entries on 3 April 2026, at temperature 0 with the canonical prompt (SHA-256 prefix 1e1cfdd99246bbf5). These pre-fills are released as silver_annotations and are not human-validated.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Human rating
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: 22 annotators, 8 of them authors of the paper, joined through an open research call and took part voluntarily without payment. They rated each pre-filled value as Correct, Partially Correct or Not Correct, with failure-mode labels, an optional corrected value, notes and a confidence level, using the paper as the source. Every cell received at least three ratings (four for 415 cells) over seven phases between 10 March and 25 April 2026, from a calibration pilot to clean-up sweeps. Ratings were collected in shared online spreadsheets, one per annotator and phase, and annotators were instructed not to use AI tools. After deduplication there are 9,595 ratings. Per-field agreement (Krippendorff's alpha, Gwet's AC1, raw agreement) is in iaa.parquet.

prov:wasAttributedTo.prov:label: 22 human annotators (pseudonyms A01 to A22)
prov:wasAttributedTo.sc:description: Master's and PhD students, postdoctoral researchers, faculty and industry or independent researchers; roster in annotators.parquet

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Gold derivation and adjudication
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Gold values were taken from the majority vote in each cell. A senior author adjudicated the 140 cells without a majority (gold_method adjudicated), and a second senior author resolved 14 cells whose last ratings arrived too late for the majority vote.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Author audit
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: An end-to-end author audit corrected 191 of the 3,060 gold cells, across 78 of the 102 entries and 25 of the 30 fields (gold_method audit_corrected_2026-05-04; adjudication_notes give the reason for each correction). The audit label replaces the earlier label of each corrected cell, including some adjudicated cells.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: System outputs
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: The 24 extraction systems ranked in the paper and the Claude Sonnet 4.5 reference were run on the 14 development and 88 test entries (system_outputs).

prov:wasAttributedTo.prov:label: 24 extraction systems and the Claude Sonnet 4.5 reference
prov:wasAttributedTo.sc:description: frontier and open-weight LLMs in single-pass extraction and four agentic architectures

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: LLM judging and judge audit
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: System outputs on the Responsible AI fields of the 88 test entries were scored by a GLM-5 judge on a three-level rubric (judge_verdicts). The judge was selected from six candidates on 60 cells, 30 for calibration and 30 for validation (judge_selection), and three authors audited it on 200 cells (judge_audit_200).

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Re-annotation pilot
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: To check the effect of the seed model, papers were re-annotated from GPT-5.4 pre-fills with the original protocol (three raters per cell, the same rubric and majority vote); the 10 test entries analysed in the paper are marked by in_paper_analysis (pilot_gold, pilot_ratings).
